Bit-vector operations

Source: R/bitvectors.R
z3_bitvectors.Rd

Bit-vectors are fixed-width machine integers. Arithmetic wraps around modulo 2^width, and the same bits can be read as unsigned or as two's complement signed numbers, so operations whose result depends on that reading come in unsigned (u) and signed (s) versions. Both operands of a binary operation must have the same width; R numbers are converted to that width and must fit in it as an unsigned or signed value.

z3_bvult(x, y)

z3_bvule(x, y)

z3_bvugt(x, y)

z3_bvuge(x, y)

z3_bvslt(x, y)

z3_bvsle(x, y)

z3_bvsgt(x, y)

z3_bvsge(x, y)

z3_bvudiv(x, y)

z3_bvsdiv(x, y)

z3_bvurem(x, y)

z3_bvsrem(x, y)

z3_bvsmod(x, y)

z3_bvand(x, y)

z3_bvor(x, y)

z3_bvxor(x, y)

z3_bvnand(x, y)

z3_bvnor(x, y)

Arguments

x, y

Bit-vector expressions (or R whole numbers for one operand).

...

Bit-vector or String expressions for z3_concat().

high, low

Bit positions, width > high >= low >= 0.

n

Number of bits or repetitions.

signed

Signed (two's complement) interpretation.

width

Bit-vector width.

i

Bit index for z3_bit2bool() (0 is the least significant bit).

ctx

A z3_context().

bits

A logical vector, least significant bit first.

Value

A z3_expr.

Details

+, -, *, ==, !=, &, | and ! work directly on bit-vectors; see z3_operators.

  • Comparisons: z3_bvult(), z3_bvule(), z3_bvugt(), z3_bvuge() (unsigned) and z3_bvslt(), z3_bvsle(), z3_bvsgt(), z3_bvsge() (signed).

  • Division: z3_bvudiv(), z3_bvurem() (unsigned); z3_bvsdiv(), z3_bvsrem() (signed, remainder has the sign of the dividend) and z3_bvsmod() (signed, remainder has the sign of the divisor). Division by zero follows SMT-LIB: bvudiv(x, 0) is all ones and bvurem(x, 0) is x.

  • Bitwise: z3_bvand(), z3_bvor(), z3_bvxor(), z3_bvnot(), z3_bvnand(), z3_bvnor(), z3_bvxnor().

  • Shifts: z3_bvshl() (left), z3_bvlshr() (logical right, fills with zeros), z3_bvashr() (arithmetic right, copies the sign bit). Rotations: z3_rotate_left(), z3_rotate_right() by a constant.

  • Width: z3_concat() joins bit-vectors (first argument in the high bits), z3_extract(x, high, low) takes bits high down to low, z3_zero_ext() and z3_sign_ext() add n bits, z3_repeat() repeats x.

  • Conversions: z3_bv2int() reads the bits as an unbounded Int, unsigned unless signed = TRUE; z3_int2bv() takes an Int modulo 2^width.

  • Overflow predicates: z3_bvadd_no_overflow() and friends are TRUE when the operation does not overflow in the given signedness.

Examples

ctx <- z3_context()
x <- z3_bv(ctx, "x", 8)
s <- z3_solver(ctx)
# 200 is negative as a signed 8-bit number
z3_add(s, x == 200, z3_bvslt(x, 0), z3_bvugt(x, 100))
z3_check(s)
#> [1] "sat"
# Overflow: x + 1 wraps around to 0
z3_simplify(z3_bv_val(ctx, 255, 8) + 1)
#> <z3_expr (_ BitVec 8)> #x00
z3_simplify(z3_extract(z3_bv_val(ctx, 0xAB, 8), 7, 4))
#> <z3_expr (_ BitVec 4)> #xa
z3_simplify(z3_bv2int(z3_bv_val(ctx, 255, 8), signed = TRUE))
#> <z3_expr Int> (- 1)
